=== page 5 ===
Mobility today is no longer just about getting from one place 
to another — it is about what that journey represents. It is an expression of aspiration, identity and responsibility. As customers seek smarter, safer and more sustainable ways to move, the role of mobility is being redefined — from a functional need to a purposeful choice.
At Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, we are responding 
to this shift with intention and clarity. We are not just building cars; we are shaping experiences that align with the evolving values of our customers — where design inspires, technology empowers, and sustainability is integral, not optional.
India stands at the forefront of this transformation 
— a market where design sensibilities are maturing, electric mobility is gaining momentum, and customer expectations are rising rapidly. In this dynamic landscape, our commitment is anchored in purpose: to create mobility solutions that are intuitive, future-ready and deeply relevant to the lives they serve.
Driven by Purpose reflects how we approach every 
dimension of our business. From reimagining product design, to advancing electrification through a robust EV portfolio, to embedding connected technologies that elevate safety and convenience — every decision is guided by a larger intent: to deliver meaningful value to our customers and stakeholders.
Our purpose extends beyond products. It shapes how we 
engage with our customers, strengthen our dealer and partner ecosystem, build capabilities within our workforce, and contribute meaningfully to the communities we serve. It guides us to create deeper, more intuitive connections — moving from transactions to relationships built on trust, transparency and delight. 
Within our organisation, it inspires a culture of continuous 
learning, innovation and accountability — equipping our people with the skills and mindset needed to lead in a rapidly evolving mobility landscape. Beyond business, it strengthens our commitment to responsible growth — advancing sustainable practices, fostering inclusivity and creating a positive social impact in every community we touch.
In essence, our purpose is not an abstract ideal — it is a 
lived commitment that informs every interaction, every decision and every action across our value chain. It drives us to empower our stakeholders as long-term collaborators in our growth journey, ensuring shared value and resilience across the ecosystem, driving us to adopt more sustainable practices across our operations and to contribute meaningfully to a cleaner, greener future.
As we move forward, this purpose will continue to define 
our path — enabling us to innovate with conviction, grow with responsibility, and create experiences that resonate far beyond the drive.
Because at Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, we are not just 
moving forward — we are Driven by Purpose.

Dear Shareholders,
It is my privilege to present the 81st Annual Report of Tata 
Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (formerly Tata Motors 
Limited) for the financial year ended March 31, 2026—our first year as an exclusive, personal mobility company. 
This milestone follows the successful demerger and 
independent public listing of the Commercial Vehicles business and the renaming of your Company as Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited, signalling our ambition to build a unique personal mobility franchise that strengthens its leadership in India’s passenger vehicles market and continues to create an exciting global presence in the modern luxury space through JLR. I would like to thank all colleagues, who contributed with commitment and rigor  to the successful execution of the demerger.
The year 2026 began with expectations of steady global 
growth, soft inflation and easier financial conditions. However, the introduction of US tariffs in May 2025 created significant challenges globally. India responded by reducing its GST rates to boost domestic consumption which helped prop up domestic growth rates in the second half of the year. The year also witnessed positive developments including the signing of the landmark India-EU and India-UK Chairman’s message 
trade agreement, US-UK and the interim India-US trade deal. However, by early March, the start of the West Asia crisis brought rising concerns about stagflation—falling output coupled with rising inflation.
India
In India, your Company delivered strong operating and financial performance in fiscal 2026.
We delivered highest-ever sales of ~6.42 lakh cars and SUVs 
during the year, achieving robust year on year growth of 15.3%, nearly twice the industry average. In the second half of the fiscal year, your Company emerged as the second largest player in the industry, with a market share of 14.1%, reflecting the growing scale, competitiveness and effectiveness of our multi-powertrain strategy.
Growth during the year was broad based, marked by a clear 
shift in customer preference and sales momentum towards greener powertrains. The strength and relevance of our product portfolio were clearly demonstrated through the following achievements:•
 Ne
xon and Punch emerging as the #1 and #3 highest 
selling models in the industry in second half of the fiscal year, reflecting growing customer preference. 
N Chandrasekaran
Chairman

i
con of the Indian automotive landscape to widespread 
acclaim and registering a strong market response with record customer bookings.

 Sa

growth, underscoring our ability to anticipate and respond to evolving customer preferences. 
•
 Re
-entry in the South African market marked a strategic 
step forward towards greater internationalisation.
Your Company remains a clear market leader in Electric Vehicles, surpassing the cumulative milestone of 250,000 EVs and commanding a dominant two thirds share of all EVs sold in India till date. In the fiscal 2026, your Company sold over 92,000 EVs marking a 43.4% growth over the previous year. The Company has been the #1 player in the market consistently for over the past 7 years with the current market share being 40.2%. 
Over the past few years, your Company has delivered 
sustained value creation- achieving growth at a CAGR of approximately 30%, with volumes expanding nearly five fold and revenues increasing close to six fold, while significantly enhancing customer access and convenience by doubling its sales and service network across the country. Your Company’s CSR initiatives continued to create meaningful impact through integrated village development, water stewardship and community resilience programmes, supported by sustained investments in skills, education and healthcare. During the year, our social interventions benefited over 18 lakh citizens across 105 districts, with over 52% of beneficiaries from marginalized communities, reinforcing our commitment to inclusive development. Key initiatives included the rejuvenation of over 1,000 water bodies across 20 districts in Maharashtra benefitting more than 6 lakh people, education programmes impacting over 2 lakh students, and targeted efforts enabling worthy aspirants to secure admissions to leading engineering and medical institutions.
The business delivered revenues of ₹58,465 crore, 
registering a healthy growth of 20.7% over FY25 with steady EBITDA and EBIT margins of 6.9% and 1.4% respectively. The PBT (bei) for the year stood at ₹1,436 crore, a 32.6% increase over FY25. The balance sheet remained robust with net cash position of ₹6,710 crore, underscoring the commitment to financial discipline while continuing to step-up on investments to deliver industry beating growth.

CHAIRMAN’S MESSAGE
Jaguar Land Rover: Resilience  
through a period of change
FY26 was a challenging year for Jaguar Land Rover, shaped 
by a confluence of internal and external disruptions. JLR was impacted by the introduction of incremental US tariffs impacting the exports from the UK to EU and the US. Additionally, the cyber incident resulted in your Company having to pause production for five weeks. These challenges reinforce the importance of resilience across strategy, vehicle architecture and powertrain choices, while needing to remain committed to technology investment. 
Revenues for the year were GBP 22,911 million down by 
20.9% compared to the previous year with results impacted by production pause due to the cyber incident. 
The year also marked a leadership transition with the 
retirement of Adrian Mardell, who dedicated 35 years to JLR and led the Company through an enormous transformation. With the appointment of PB Balaji as the CEO, JLR will continue to build on strong foundations as it enters its next phase of growth.
Consolidated Financials:  On a consolidated basis, the business 
delivered revenues of ₹335,582 crore and PBT (bei) of ₹2,519 
crore for the year. The consolidated financial metrics for the year were impacted due multiple headwinds at JLR, including the production pause for five weeks due to the cyber incident. However, with return to normalcy of production and the continued demand momentum in the India PV business, the Company delivered a strong quarter in Q4FY26 with revenues of ₹105,447 crore and PBT (bei) of ₹7,167 crore.    
The Board of Directors have recommended a final dividend of 
₹3/- per share for Fiscal 26, subject to your approval.
Trends shaping mobility  
Rapid global advances in digital technologies and AI are transforming how mobility products are designed, experienced and supported. At the same time, the transition to clean energy, heightened expectations on safety, and the reconfiguration of global supply chains are redefining competitiveness. Geopolitical and uneven economic recovery are adding further complexity, making agility and resilience critical capabilities. 
India’s mobility transition is being shaped by—aspiration, 
infrastructure and evolving consumer expectations. The sustained demand supports the ICE portfolio and the continued momentum in EVs reflects growing customer confidence in new technologies underscoring the strength of a balanced, multi powertrain strategy of your Company. Looking ahead
We enter FY27 with confidence, supported by a robust pipeline of new launches and multi-powertrain offerings. Our focus will remain on delivering industry-leading growth, deepening our commitment to safety, sustainability, quality and customer delight, while becoming resilient and staying agile amid macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties. 
Your Company will continue to focus on building 
distinctive, trusted and aspirational brands that connect meaningfully with customers. For Jaguar Land Rover, this is embodied in its House of Brands strategy, creating sharply differentiated luxury brands with clear identities, purpose and desirability. JLR will additionally focus on reducing its breakeven levels which has been impacted by tariffs, currency and commodities inflation, back to 300K units in the next 2 years whilst remaining focused on delivering exceptional launches of its New Range Rover Electric, Jaguar Type 01 and continue to build its Modern Luxury franchise. At Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, this thinking is reflected in the introduction of a more purposeful brand proposition, sharpening our focus on aspiration, trust and customer centricity. 
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Jaguar Land Rover will 
continue to collaborate on manufacturing, technology and people, enhancing scale efficiencies, accelerating learning and reinforcing capital discipline. Early progress is evident with the commencement of operations at the new Panapakkam facility in Tamil Nadu, creating a shared manufacturing facility for best practice execution and scale benefits. 
Your Company will continue to embed digital technologies and 
AI across the value chain, build strong advanced analytics and leverage connected technologies to deliver personalised and proactive customer engagement. 
Guided by Project Aalingana, the Tata Group’s vision for a 
greener, cleaner and more equitable future, sustainability remains integral to your Company. With electrification at the core of substantiality, we are committed to being Net Zero by 2040. Your Company will continue to invest in products, platforms and ecosystems for accessible and scalable zero emission mobility solutions, while continuing to improve conventional powertrains.
On behalf of the Board, I would like to thank the employees, 
customers, suppliers and shareholders, for your continued trust and support. We are committed to moving forward with confidence in our strategy, optimism about our opportunities, and a strong focus on creating long-term value.
Warm Regards,
N Chandrasekaran

Operating environment 
The automotive industry is operating in a dynamic and complex environment 
shaped by evolving consumer preferences, heightened competition, shortening product cycles, regulatory shifts and policy divergence, cost pressures and geopolitical uncertainties. 
These factors have added layers of complexity and growth opportunities, which 
players will need to navigate with increasing agility and strategic clarity to win. 
Resilient  
business strategy
In today’s world, automotive OEMs are increasingly 
adopting resilient, flexible business strategies anchored around portfolio diversification, multi powertrain offerings, and agile operating models to succeed across markets. A balanced portfolio approach covering future-ready powertrains is becoming increasingly more important to address a wider spectrum of customer needs. At the same time, strategic localisation, supplier diversification and proactive risk management are becoming critical to strengthening supply chain resilience. Simultaneously, disciplined cost management, value engineering and scalable platforms are emerging as key imperatives to enable manufacturers to strengthen margins and remain competitive despite uncertainties. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited is strengthening resilience through a diversified product portfolio, multi powertrain strategy, localised and agile operating models, and disciplined cost and risk management to navigate uncertainties while supporting sustainable growth. In FY26, in a tough competitive environment, the domestic business delivered highest ever volumes and became #2 player in H2 through multiple product interventions and agile actions to manage demand post GST 2.0 rollout. JLR is evolving its operating model to further centre around its House of Brands, growing each brand’s distinct identity and value to increase desirability and emotional connection with its clients. JLR has deployed a flexible powertrain approach to manage the slower-than-expected transition to electrification, offering a mix of ICE, PHEV and soon to be BEV powertrain options on its MLA platform.

Future ready technology and  
digital transformationSustainability  
and ESG
Sustainability and ESG considerations are now 
integral to the automotive industry’s strategic and manufacturing agenda, as a key value driver, and to address the imperatives for the globe. There is a definite transition towards greener and zero emission mobility, led by greater OEM participation and rising customer acceptance. Simultaneously, OEMs are intensifying focus on sustainable manufacturing through renewable energy adoption, water and waste management, circularity, responsible sourcing  and higher localisation. 
In alignment with the Tata Group’s ‘Aalingana’ 
initiative, which focuses on achieving net-zero emissions, fostering circular economies, and preserving biodiversity, we continue to embed sustainability across our strategy and operations, with a sustained focus on cleaner mobility solutions, responsible manufacturing practices and value chain stewardship aligned with long term environmental priorities. 
We have set ambitious targets: 
achieving Net Zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2039 for JLR, and by 2040 for our Passenger Vehicles business.Technology and digital transformation are emerging 
as core enablers of competitiveness in the automotive industry. Rapid advances in software defined vehicles, connected services, ADAS, electrification and intelligent manufacturing are reshaping both products and operations. OEMs are increasingly leveraging digital tools, data analytics and artificial intelligence across design, supply chains, manufacturing and customer engagement to enhance speed, quality and efficiency. Over the air updates, connected ecosystems and digitally integrated ownership journeys are increasingly influencing purchase decisions, making software capability and digital maturity key differentiators  
for future readiness. 
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited is 
progressively building strong capabilities in SDV, connected technologies, advanced electronics and a digitally enabled value chain, to enhance product competitiveness and deliver an integrated, future-ready customer experience. The t.idal architecture will underpin the next generation vehicles with SDV capabilities, over-the-air updates, and host of connected features. Work with JLR’s key partner NVIDIA continued at global engineering hubs, developing driver assistance systems and artificial intelligence (AI) for next generation electric vehicles built on the NVIDIA DRIVE™ software defined platform. Other transformative digital initiatives include, working with strategic partners like NVIDIA to explore the capability for digital twins of manufacturing sites, and NVIDIA’s Omniverse is also being deployed to optimise designs in real time adjusting the geometry and features of a vehicle design to speed up the development process.

Message from MD & CEO, TMPVL & TPEML 
Dear Shareholders,
I hope this letter finds you in good health and spirits.
FY26 was a defining year for your Company, marked by 
the successful carving out of the commercial vehicles business and its subsequent independent listing on the stock exchanges. This milestone has transitioned your Company into a focused, standalone passenger vehicles entity with a sharper strategic focus, stronger governance, and greater flexibility in capital allocation, enabling us to pursue customer-centric growth with enhanced agility, rigor and accountability.
I am pleased to present this Annual Report with the business 
emerging stronger, financial performance improving and the Company becoming more resilient. I take this opportunity to share the progress we made during the year and outline the strategic priorities that will guide us as we move forward.
Industry overview
FY26 marked a year of recovery and renewed momentum for the Indian Passenger Vehicle (PV) industry, with record sales volumes of nearly 4.7 million units. After a period of moderation in the first half, the year witnessed a sharp rebound in the latter half, supported by policy tailwinds such as GST 2.0, strong macroeconomic fundamentals, and a buoyant festive season. The underlying demand environment remained resilient, reflecting sustained consumer confidence and aspirations. 
The passenger vehicle industry grew 8% over FY25 and 
this growth was broad-based across vehicle segments. SUVs continued to be the preferred body style, accounting for over 56% of total industry volumes. The year also saw sustained traction for greener powertrains with the CNG segment maintaining its secular growth trajectory with over 20% year on year growth and EV sales recording a sharper acceleration and crossing 2 lakh units, driven by wider OEM participation, improving value propositions, and growing customer confidence. As the industry evolves further, demand for aspirational, safe, smart, and sustainable mobility continues to gain momentum.
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles performance
Your Company navigated the year with agility and a growth focused mindset, making steady progress on its strategic priorities while strengthening the foundations for long-term, sustainable growth. Our performance this year was driven by a series of deliberate interventions across portfolio, driving electrification, customer experience and operating discipline. In parallel, we continued to advance our sustainability commitments and deepen our engagement Shailesh Chandra

MESSAGE FROM MD & CEO
Advancing electric mobility
Our EV journey marked a defining step this year as we crossed 
2.5 lakh cumulative sales. Through the year, our decisive focus was towards mainstreaming EVs by systematically and holistically addressing the barriers to their adoption.
We did this by re-engineering the value proposition of 
our EVs, bringing their acquisition costs closer to their ICE equivalents, enhancing range, improving charging speeds, and strengthening ownership confidence through initiatives such as lifetime battery warranty. Launches like Harrier.ev and New Punch.ev reflect this approach, combining aspiration with practicality to appeal to a wider set of customers.
In parallel, we scaled the charging ecosystem, expanding 
charging access through partnerships with charge point operators and our own Tata.ev Mega Charging Hubs, while improving reliability through verified charging solutions.
This integrated push across product and ecosystem drove 
over 43% year-on-year growth, with EV volumes exceeding 92,000 units, as we sustained clear market leadership with  
a 40.2% share.
Customer experience and brand trust
Enhancing customer experience and delivering sustained customer delight remains a core priority for our business. To that end, our sales outreach was broadened significantly this year, with over 100 new outlets added to reach a wider set of buyers across geographies. We also accelerated the expansion of our service footprint, adding 1,600 new workshop bays and strengthening existing facilities with digitised diagnostic and technical support capabilities. Collectively, these initiatives improved responsiveness across touchpoints, strengthened product quality, and elevated the overall ownership experience, reflected in  a rise in our Net Promoter Score to 52.
Manufacturing and supply chain readiness
Aligned with growing demand for our products, we made significant progress in strengthening and modernising our manufacturing footprint. Alongside capacity augmentation and increased digitisation across existing plants, we commenced operations at our new joint manufacturing facility with Jaguar Land Rover in Tamil Nadu, enhancing our readiness for future growth. We also deepened the deployment of artificial intelligence across our operations, leveraging it to drive improvements in product quality, enhance manufacturing efficiency, and strengthen workforce safety. In parallel, we continued to build increasingly localised, agile, high quality, and robust supply chains to support scale and resilience as we navigate a complex geopolitical climate.Embedding sustainability
Sustainability continues to be embedded deeply across our operations and decision making as we advance toward our goal of achieving Net Zero emissions by 2040. During the year, we reduced our carbon footprint across the value chain through higher adoption of renewable energy, increased penetration of greener powertrains, and cross-deployment of best practices. We also progressed on broader environmental priorities, including circularity and biodiversity, with clear pathways and governance frameworks now in place.
Advancing community wellbeing
Our commitment to social responsibility remained steadfast through the year, with CSR programmes delivering tangible outcomes across our operating regions. We continued to invest in water stewardship and the rejuvenation of community water bodies, strengthening both livelihoods and environmental sustainability. Alongside, our focus on skill development, education, and healthcare access helped drive meaningful change in the communities around us, further amplified by active employee volunteering participation. These efforts reinforce our conviction that building a responsible and sustainable business goes well beyond the factory floor.
Looking ahead
While the industry will need to closely monitor ongoing geopolitical developments, the fundamental demand drivers of the Indian passenger vehicles market remain strong, with growth expected to be led by SUV, CNG, and EV segments. We enter FY27 with confidence, supported by stronger fundamentals, a robust pipeline of new launches, multi powertrain offerings, and renewed momentum from the second half of FY26. Our focus will remain on delivering industry leading growth while deepening our commitment to safety, sustainability, quality, and customer delight. At the same time, we will continue to ensure agility and resilience in our execution as we navigate the geopolitical environment. 
I remain confident that your Company is well positioned to 
create long term value for all stakeholders. This confidence is founded on the passion, resilience and talent of our people, and the enduring trust that our customers and you, our shareholders, place in us. Thank you for your continued support and belief in our journey.
Warm regards,
Shailesh Chandra

External environment
Robust industry growth in H2 post GST 2.0
After a slow start in H1, where growth rates were flat, the 
PV industry saw a sharp rebound in demand post GST 2.0 in September 2025. Reduced GST rates resulted in improved affordability which helped drive demand across segments, resulting in strong double-digit growth in H2 FY26. As a result, the industry saw record annual volumes of over 4.7 million units for FY26, and will head into FY27 with significant demand momentum. 
Key transitions in bodystyle and 
technology preferences 
Post GST 2.0, industry growth has been disproportionately 
strong in Sub Compact, Compact, and Mid SUVs, reinforcing India’s sustained preference for the SUV bodystyle. Additionally, there was strong growth in greener powertrains, i.e. CNG vehicles & EVs, reflecting growing customer preference. Simultaneously, customer expectations for in vehicle technology have risen sharply across segments. Entry categories increasingly demand richer feature sets, while higher segments are adopting advanced systems including ADAS suites, auto park assist etc., which are setting new benchmarks in premium mobility. Safety has also become a decisive purchase criterion, with rising consumer preference for 5 star rated vehicles and models equipped with comprehensive active and passive safety systems.
EV momentum strengthens on OEM 
participation and ecosystem maturity 
EV adoption accelerated in FY26, supported by the 
continued 5% GST for EVs and strong OEM participation. New high aspiration EV launches expanded category consideration, while coordinated marketing efforts by OEMs helped build awareness and reinforce customer confidence. At the same time, charging infrastructure surpassed over 30,000 public charging stations improving in reliability, highway coverability, and residential accessibility, making ownership more seamless. These developments collectively strengthened EV momentum and positioned EVs as an expanding and structurally important part of India’s powertrain landscape.

Message from CEO - JLR 
Dear Shareholders,
While JLR made strong operational progress in FY26, including 
the development of our next-generation models and the continued growth of our unique modern luxury brands, it was a year marked by challenges. 
In the first quarter, we faced a hike in costs from incremental 
trade tariffs of 27.5% on our UK and EU exports to the US. These were later reduced to 10% and 15% respectively, where they now remain. In the second quarter, we proactively shut down our systems as a precautionary measure in response to the cyber incident. Production was paused before restarting on  
8 October and returning to normal levels by mid-November.
I am extremely proud of our teams’ professional and focused 
responses to these hurdles. 
These challenges arrived with the global automotive industry 
already under continued pressure from cost inflation, slower-than-expected uptake of electric vehicles, and the deterioration of market conditions in China, including the lowering of the threshold for the luxury car tax which affected pricing. 
Financially, we delivered a profitable first quarter, the US trade 
tariffs and the cyber incident impacted Q2 and Q3, and our performance stabilised in Q4 with quarterly revenues of  
£6.9b, a profit before tax of £452 million, and EBIT of 9.2%. Over the full financial year, JLR recorded revenues of £22.9b and adjusted EBIT of 0.7% demonstrating the Company’s robust underpinnings and the continued desirability of our luxury brands.
This year, we made significant progress across our operations. 
Range Rover featured in the Top 100 Global Brands for the second consecutive year, and Range Rover Electric won critical acclaim from global media, who took part in prototype drives.
Excitement continued to build around new Jaguar, with the 
Type 00 design concept progressing its global tour. The car featured in Monaco, Tokyo and London, and the world’s motoring journalists responded positively to passenger drives  
in the new Jaguar prototype vehicles.
Defender won the 2026 Dakar Rally in the Stock class, with 
its Defender OCTA derived Dakar D7X-R vehicles placing first and second. This represented an outstanding accomplishment for the team in Defender’s debut year at Dakar, the world’s toughest off-road challenge, and demonstrated Defender’s unrivalled off-road capabilities.
Meanwhile, the transformation of our global manufacturing 
facilities to enable electric vehicle production alongside internal combustion engine (ICE) and hybrid variants neared completion, and we announced nearly £100 million in value from reuse and refurbishment initiatives at our UK and European plants.

Geopolitics 
Evolving regulatory frameworks, including use of further tariff and non-tariff protectionism mechanisms as well as conflicts, such as that in the Middle East would have a material adverse effect on our business prospects, results and financial condition. The secondary consequences of such geopolitical events may include further financial instability and slower economic growth in the UK, continental Europe and globally. They could also impact our supply chains or otherwise constrain our ability to operate efficiently.
Despite having manufacturing sites around the world, our 
primary activities are in the UK and Europe and are vulnerable to changes in trade tariffs. Although smaller in terms of overall volume, our other manufacturing facilities located around the rest of the world, including China, India and Brazil, could also be vulnerable to shifts in global trade and economic policies, and the fallout from the conflict in the Middle East.. Any adverse changes to tariff policies on a global basis could have a material adverse effect on our business prospects, results of operations and financial condition. 
During 2025, we experienced the effect of this through 
incremental US tariffs applied to our exports from the UK and EU. Subsequent trade deals between the UK and US and the EU and US as well as the relaxation of the US emission regulations have reduced the impact on the business, but they continue to add to the cost and uncertainty of doing business in the US.
Demand and competition
Consumer demand continues to be affected by uncertainty surrounding electric vehicles, particularly concerns related to range, the availability of charging infrastructure and lower residual values. High upfront costs for vehicle purchases and home charging installation, combined with fluctuating government incentives, further contribute to hesitation and delays among potential buyers.
In addition, market conditions are becoming more 
challenging because of increased competition, especially from Chinese manufacturers in UK and European markets. The introduction of the China Luxury Tax has added further pressure in the local China market, making higher value vehicles even more expensive for consumers or adding pressure on margins for OEMs through additional discounting in China and other regions where they try to reallocate production.
Supply chain risks 
The automotive requirement for rare earth elements and other specialised materials in electric vehicle production presents a significant critical-mineral supply risk. Additionally, natural disasters and human driven events, such as labour disputes, have the potential to disrupt the just-in-time manufacturing process, creating further supply chain vulnerabilities.
Cyber 
Cybersecurity risks remain elevated, as malicious actors continue to target all types of organisations and cause disruption, as we experienced in 2025. As products and services across all industries become more technologically advanced and connected, cybersecurity considerations remain an evolving area of focus for businesses. These global cybersecurity risks range from isolated, uncoordinated attempts to highly sophisticated and targeted attacks, referred to as advanced persistent threats.Challenges

Research & Development continued extensively across 
multiple fronts at JLR. In pursuit of reducing the carbon footprint of key vehicle structural elements, the Company successfully reengineered the crosscar beam – which sits behind the dashboard – using a hybrid solution of fibre reinforced plastic and steel. 
By removing the carbon intensive 
magnesium from this element, the carefully tested innovation is projected to cut over 50,000 tonnes of CO₂ annually, which is equivalent to the average yearly energy use of approximately 17,000 UK homes.
In next generation propulsion technology, JLR expanded 
its research into the use of recycled critical minerals in battery cells in collaboration with Warwick Manufacturing 
JLR
Group (WMG) and UK clean technology companies such as Altilium. Part of the UK Government’s Drive35 grant funding, the latest project will see the partners produce and test multi-layer pouch cells containing both cathode and anode materials recovered from end-of-life EV batteries, exploring ways to process high-value materials for integration into next-generation battery production, reducing reliance on imported materials and cutting carbon emissions.
JLR continued to strengthen its house of brands through 
disciplined engineering and product development. Range Rover Electric testing and validation advanced with another round of durability testing, including a second full Arctic Circle campaign covering more than 45,000 miles. These evaluations validated core technologies such as the ThermAssist™ thermal management system, designed to enhance energy efficiency and charging performance in extreme cold, while also refining dynamic capability, single pedal driving and next generation air suspension systems. This rigorous approach ensures the vehicle meets the highest standards of refinement and capability expected by Range Rover owners.

SDV architecture, t.idal, which will underpin upcoming product launches. We are collaborating closely with key partners and have established a clear, phased roadmap for our SDV transition. During the year, JLR also reached a new milestone 
in Software Over the Air (SOTA) updates, with over 31 million updates issued to over two million vehicles globally since 2020, covering infotainment and connectivity, assisted and autonomous driving, body systems & software, powertrain and chassis. Capability to deploy SOTA and Features Over the Air (FOTA) will rapidly expand over the remainder of the decade as JLR launches its next generation vehicles, as JLR takes advantage of partnership with Tata Communications and leverages the MOVE™ platform to enable greater and more secure data exchange between JLR and clients’ vehicles. Safety has been a cornerstone of TMPVL since inception. 
The establishment of an in house crash testing facility at the very outset reflected a clear belief that safety must be engineered into vehicles from the first sketch, not added as an afterthought. Over the years, this philosophy has become deeply embedded in our DNA, guiding product design, engineering choices, and manufacturing processes. 
During the year, all our major launches—the new Altroz, 
Harrier.ev, Sierra and Punch—achieved 5 star ratings under Bharat NCAP, reinforcing the consistent safety performance of our portfolio. 
In our recent launches, we have gone beyond ratings 
and protocols to demonstrate safety in real world crash scenarios. The Sierra showcased structural integrity and occupant protection in a car to car collision, while the Punch demonstrated robustness in a car to truck impact. These representations underscore our belief in delivering true safety to all of our customers. For decades, JLR has pioneered safety innovation - from Jaguar’s introduction of disc brakes in the 1950s to Freelander’s Hill Descent Control in the 1990s, and more recently, pioneering adaptive off road cruise control in the latest Range Rover Sport. These milestones reflect a long-standing commitment to engineering technologies that enhance driver capability and confidence across all terrains.
Today, each JLR brand integrates a comprehensive 
suite of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) - such as lane keep assist, automatic emergency braking and adaptive cruise control - designed to improve safety, situational awareness and enjoyment. To support drivers’ awareness levels, JLR has also recently deployed new Driver Attention Monitor cameras across its models to monitor a driver’s gaze and provide adjustable audio visual alerts to help ensure they are paying attention to the road.
JLR’s most recent 13 models have been certified 
with 5-star Euro NCAP ratings. JLR uses crash dummies of all shapes and sizes, a long-standing practice to ensure vehicle safety mirrors the different physical traits of its clients. The Company is also working with startups to improve vehicle safety, such as Allfocal Optics, to integrate nanophotic lens technology into its Head Up Displays (HUDs) – by projecting images directly onto the retina, this form of augmented reality could enhance navigation and safety.JLR3Safety
We remain committed to  safety, through active and passive 
safety systems, with the aim of making safety accessible, intuitive and uncompromising across our portfolio.

TMPVL’s Panapakkam plant brings together advanced

JLR is also modernising its long standing mainframe

Materiality  
assessment 
At Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited, 
we acknowledge the role of materiality assessments in ensuring that our ESG efforts remain relevant, strategic, and impactful. Last year, we broadened our approach to materiality assessments by incorporating the concept of double materiality for the first time.
The double materiality assessment (DMA) has helped us 
determine which sustainability issues are most important to the organisation and its stakeholders. It involves evaluating the organisation’s impact on environmental and social factors (inside-out perspective) and examining how these factors affect the organisation (outside-in perspective). This dual approach helps the Company identify and prioritise ESG issues that are both financially important and socially significant, promoting the comprehensive integration of sustainability into its core strategy. We plan to conduct similar assessments every two years, taking emerging sustainability issues, global events and other trends into consideration.TMPVL identified relevant ESG material topics, through stakeholder consultations, evaluation of ESG frameworks, and an assessment of the maturity of the organisation’s current practices.
For each identified topic, the related 
impacts, risks, and opportunities (IROs) were developed across TMPVL’s value chain, informed by research on past events and forecasts made by think tanks and academia.
Identification  TMPVL
1
2
An impact and financial assessment were 
conducted for each IRO, following the Double Materiality methodology. The impacts were assessed based on their scale, scope, irremediability, and likelihood, while the risks and opportunities were evaluated in terms of their magnitude and likelihood.
TMPVL internal and external stakeholders 
reviewed the IROs and their associated scores to evaluate their significance and completeness. Adjustments were made based on the feedback received from the stakeholders.Assessment
3
4
A final materiality matrix was created based 
on the scores. A scoring threshold was established to identify high-priority topics, which were then further reviewed and confirmed by senior management.Determination

1 Driving net zero
The climate crisis is no longer a distant risk; it is a defining 
reality of our time. FY26 has reinforced our resolve to transform how we move people, how we build products, and how we engage with the planet. As the world accelerates toward clean energy, circular systems, and climate
-re
silient 
business models, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited is not only adapting but also setting the direction for the industry.
Guided by science and driven by purpose, we are advancing 
a bold decarbonisation journey and remain firmly on track to achieve Net Zero emissions by 2040. 
Our commitment to RE100 continues to gather momentum, 
supported by a clear roadmap to power all our operations with 100% renewable electricity by 2030.
FY26 marked a year of decisive action, reflected in the 
products we launched, the technologies we deployed, and the partnerships we strengthened to translate sustainable mobility from ambition into reality.
Our emissions  
reduction strategy
Our decarbonisation journey is holistic and structured, spanning all three scopes of emissions (Scope 1,2, and 3) and unfolding across short
-, m
edium -, a
nd long -te
rm horizons. 
Together, these actions define a clear and credible pathway  
to Net Zero.
In the near term, up to 2030, our Scope 2 priority is clear: 
achieving RE100 by sourcing 100% of our operational electricity from renewable electricity. As an RE100 signatory, this commitment is supported by a defined roadmap that includes on
-si
te renewable installations, power purchase 
agreements, and the use of energy attribute certificates. In parallel, we are systematically reducing our reliance on conventional energy sources across our operations through the ENCON programme and targeted efficiency interventions, enabling a progressive reduction in our Scope 1 emissions. For Scope 3, our near
-te
rm actions are guided by scientifically 
aligned decarbonisation trajectories. Targets defined through these trajectories directly shape our product portfolio decisions, accelerating the transition to low
- a
nd zero -emi
ssion 
vehicle technologies and establishing a strong foundation for a Net Zero future.
Over the medium term, up to 2035, the focus shifts 
to eliminating residual Scope 1 emissions through the electrification of fuel
-de
pendent operational assets, including 
energy -int
ensive processes such as paint shops. This transition 
will steadily move our direct emissions profile toward zero. Concurrently, we will consolidate and accelerate the transition to Zero Emission Vehicles across our Passenger Vehicle portfolio, driving a substantial reduction in Scope 3 emissions.
In the long term, our strategy is anchored in destination 
technologies for the segment, with Battery Electric Vehicles forming the cornerstone of our Passenger Vehicle roadmap. As these technologies achieve widespread market adoption, they will be complemented by significant reductions in upstream supply chain emissions, particularly Scope 3 Category 1. Together, these efforts position us to fulfil our Net Zero ambition for the Passenger Vehicles business by 2040.

Energy management  
Energy management is central to our operational 
philosophy, and its importance has only intensified in today’s evolving geopolitical and energy landscape. Guided by India’s enduring ethos of resource optimisation, we strive to do more with less, enhancing efficiency while minimising environmental impact. By systematically reducing energy consumption, we not only advance our sustainability ambitions but also unlock a significant cost advantage, as improved energy efficiency directly lowers the variable cost of production. Our structured Energy Conservation (ENCON) initiatives are key enablers in this journey, optimising the use of power and fuels while delivering measurable cost savings and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Additionally, lower energy demand supports a smooth transition to renewables, as reduced consumption translates into lower capacity requirements and more efficient investments in clean energy infrastructure.
To sustain and accelerate these efforts, we rely on a robust 
framework of internal audits and continuous performance monitoring to identify opportunities for improvement. These assessments guide targeted interventions, technology upgrades, and process innovations that enhance energy efficiency across our operations. Supported by clear, measurable targets aligned with our broader sustainability goals, this disciplined approach ensures ongoing progress, strengthening operational resilience, improving cost competitiveness, and reinforcing our commitment to a low-carbon future.

2.1 Circularity through design
We are committed to strengthening circularity in its 
vehicles by embedding design-for-circularity principles including enablement of ease of dismantling, and prioritising sustainable material choices to enhance the overall circularity of its products.
The Company is progressively adopting modular design 
approaches that support efficient disassembly, component reuse, and remanufacturing, thereby reducing waste and environmental impact across the vehicle lifecycle. To facilitate responsible end-of-life management, dismantling information for 11 existing and phased-out models has been published on the International Dismantling Information System (IDIS), enabling dismantlers to safely manage vehicle disposal.
Over 90% of the materials used in our vehicles are recyclable 
and recoverable. The vehicles also incorporate recycled content across materials such as steel, aluminium, glass, and polymers, with average recycled content ranging between 7–8% across both ICE and EV models. The Company is further developing closed-loop recycling systems for key materials such as metals, glass, plastics, and oil to reduce reliance on virgin resources and enhance material circularity.

Life Cycle Assessments (LCAs)
In line with its commitment to Sustainability, we conduct 
comprehensive Life Cycle Assessments (LCAs) to evaluate the environmental impacts of its products. These assessments examine resource use, ecological impacts such as greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and ecotoxicity, as well as human health considerations including human toxicity and ionising radiation. LCAs quantify these impacts using established indicators such as Global Warming Potential, Acidification Potential, Eutrophication Potential, Abiotic Depletion, Ozone Layer Depletion, and Photochemical Ozone Creation Potential.
Cradle-to-Grave LCA has been completed for the Nexon 
ICE and EV variants, with third-party validation. In addition, Cradle-to-Gate internal LCA assessments have been conducted for multiple passenger vehicle models, including Tiago, Tigor, Punch, Nexon, Curvv, Harrier MCE, Safari MCE, Sierra, Tiago EV, Tigor EV, Nexon EV, Punch EV, Curvv EV, and Harrier EV.
To better understand the lifecycle impacts of EV battery 
cells, a Cradle-to-Gate analysis was also conducted with the support of a third-party consultant. This study evaluates the global supply-chain impacts of battery manufacturing, including the influence of different manufacturing locations, such as China and India.
These LCA studies help in identification of ‘hotspots’ where 
environmental impacts are most significant, enabling targeted improvements to reduce product carbon footprint, minimise waste generation and promote use of sustainable materials. We have systematically embedded these objectives in our product development process by setting decarbonisation and material circularity targets for future passenger vehicle models.
Nexon ICE & EV - An LCA landmark:
Building on the earlier Cradle-to-Grave Life Cycle Assessment of the Tata Nexon Diesel variant, the Company has now completed a comprehensive and independently verified LCA for the Nexon EV across different battery capacities, setting  a new benchmark in its sustainability practices.
The study, conducted in accordance with ISO 14040 and 
ISO 14044 standards, evaluates environmental impacts across the vehicle’s entire lifecycle, covering all stages from raw material extraction through manufacturing and use to end-of-life treatment. This comprehensive environmental impact assessment is based on vehicle-level part material distribution, detailed mapping of all part manufacturing processes, and evaluation of upstream and downstream logistics. It also incorporates plant-level vehicle manufacturing emissions, well-to-tank and tank-to-wheel emissions, and end-of-life impacts derived from emission and resource consumption data from Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facilities (RVSFs).
The study has been independently verified by M/s TÜV 
Rheinland, enhancing the robustness and credibility of the methodology, results, and conclusions. The system boundary considered in the baseline study is illustrated in the accompanying figure.Cradle to Grave Covered through scenario analysis System boundary Raw material extraction

2.3 Waste management
We are committed to advancing our Zero Waste to Landfill 
(ZWtL) by 2030 ambition across all three manufacturing facilities in Maharashtra and Gujarat, reinforcing its focus on resource efficiency, circularity, and responsible environmental stewardship.
To drive this agenda, we have adopted a structured approach 
encompassing waste baseline assessment, identification of sustainable waste diversion pathways, and third-party certification. Comprehensive waste management systems have been institutionalised across our operations covering hazardous, non-hazardous, biodegradable, recyclable, and non-recyclable waste streams. These systems are designed to proper segregation, recovery, recycling, composting, and co-processing, while ensuring compliance with all applicable regulatory requirements.Dedicated interventions, including the use of an Organic Waste Composter (OWC) at the Sanand facilities, further support the conversion of biodegradable waste into value-added compost for on-site/offsite greenbelt usage.
Over the past three years, we have made significant progress 
in advancing its circularity and waste management agenda, with all three plants securing the prestigious Confederation of Indian Industry – Green Business Centre (CII-GBC) Zero Waste to Landfill certification. We achieved an overall waste diversion rate of 99.9%, underscoring its strong commitment to sustainable manufacturing, resource efficiency, and circular economy-led operations.

2.4 Water management
We have embarked on a structured Water Neutrality 
Journey as part of our broader sustainability roadmap, with a commitment to achieve water neutrality by 2030 to strengthen long-term water security, enhance resource efficiency, and reduce our environmental footprint.
As a first step, we undertook a detailed water baseline 
assessment across all plants to evaluate freshwater consumption, water intensity across manufacturing operations, recycling potential, and site-specific water risks. These insights helped define focused interventions around water reduction, reuse, recycling, and replenishment.
We have prioritised freshwater demand reduction through 
process optimisation, improved utility management, efficient fixtures, leakage control, and enhanced monitoring systems. These measures have contributed to a reduction in water intensity per vehicle produced. We have also strengthened its water recycling and reuse infrastructure through treatment systems such as Reverse Osmosis (RO) plants, Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs), and associated recycling technologies, enabling treated water to be reused across utilities, cooling systems, and landscaping.

3 Preserving nature and biodiversity
Our biodiversity strategy is aligned with the Group’s 
Aalingana strategy, metrics and milestones, and puts in place an Action Plan for delivering a Net Positive Impact on biodiversity. At an enterprise level, the strategy lays down the steps to restore, enhance, and protect nature, ensuring  a net positive outcome on biodiversity.
Our understanding of biodiversity and species extinction 
began with the senior leadership engaging with leading Subject Matter Experts and conservation practitioners, which helped to adopt a science-based approach as opposed to the ad-hoc actions. Strategic coherence led to the identification of 3 areas for biodiversity interventions which span (1) its own Operations, (2) its Value Chain and (3) beyond the Value Chain extending to the national landscape and aligning with national conservation priorities. For each of these areas, we adopted scientific frameworks and concepts, built ambition in line with our aspiration to move the needle and established baselines.
Through FY25 to FY26, we launched projects across all 
3 areas, which have strategic relevance and potential to deliver impact at scale. The projects are conceptualised to deliver scientifically validated approaches (as SOP’s) ready for implementation; for example eco-restoration of disturbed habitats or improving the health of threatened wetlands. Such initiatives, which leverage nature and productive ecosystems to protect people and biodiversity, constitute what are called Nature based Solution (NbS) projects. In the scale-up phase of this unique strategic approach, we plan to engage Value Chain partners and corporate peers, to adopt and implement these SOPs in similar landscapes, while continuing to provide stewardship, enable convergence funding and monitor impact. This strategy will realise ours and the Groups objective of investing in NbS projects in India to deliver biodiversity and community co-benefits.
3.1 Own operations
Since inception, all our Operational sites in India  
have demarcated dedicated areas on which green-belt and wetlands are developed. A comprehensive biodiversity baseline survey across all our plants was carried out to get an in-depth understanding of floristic and faunal diversity, extent of threats, presence of species with special conservation value and other challenges. This was followed by LiDAR based drone survey to map habitats, contours, surface water flow and other geographic features required for ecosystem restoration planning.  In FY26, a comprehensive eco-restoration master plan supported by scientific metrics is being developed for execution in next FY. The eco-restoration projects are structured to meet the criteria laid down in the MoEFCC-NBA-UNDP backed OECM framework (i.e. Other Effective Area Based Conservation Measures) – which expands the scope of area-based conservation beyond legally protected areas. Going beyond certification, these Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited ‘nature hot-spots’ set in the midst of industrial estates, will serve as a lighthouse of best practice in biodiversity conservation. We are engaging our employees and local stakeholders enabling awareness-building, research, and adoption to create a ripple effect far beyond its premises. At our recently inaugurated Panapakkam facility, a one-year seasonal baseline biodiversity assessment was conducted for integrating biodiversity conservation elements into operations and campus management. 
3.2 Value chain
Automobile manufacturing sources a diverse range of parts, materials and consumables from a complex global supply chain. This sourcing determines the level of both dependency and impact on nature and natural resources. To address this, we have been working on the corporate engagement programme of Science-Based Targets for Nature. This structured approach will help us reduce our contribution to key drivers of nature loss. In FY26, we have identified material impacts of our operations and those of our immediate upstream value chain on nature and biodiversity.
3.3 Beyond value chain
We are demonstrating leadership by addressing Nature and Biodiversity beyond its Operations and Value Chain in line with our ambition to create impact at scale. After evaluating a wide range of potential topics, we shortlisted 3 projects aligned with the Kunming Montreal-Global Biodiversity Framework.
1.

 M
aximus – Asian elephants are India’s national heritage

  In J

This NbS project will deliver restoration of degraded lands which builds ecological resilience and secures livelihoods of indigenous communities that rely on forests for sustenance and cultural practices.

Workforce, talent & skills  
Kaushalya programme
The Kaushalya programme – Earn While 
Learn – is a first-of-its-kind initiative in the industry and the country, designed to transform the lives of young talent from rural India into confident, industry-ready professionals.
What began as a skilling intervention has today evolved into 
a powerful movement of inclusion and empowerment. Over 12,000 youth from rural backgrounds have been enrolled across our plants, with a strong focus on diversity—18% gender representation and 25% representation from Affirmative Action (AA)—ensuring that opportunity reaches those who need it the most. Open to 12
th/HSC/ITI 
graduates, Kaushalya goes beyond conventional training. It uniquely blends on-the-job practical experience with a fully sponsored 2-3-year Diploma in Mechatronics Engineering from reputed universities, enabling participants to earn while they learn. This integrated model ensures that learning is not just theoretical but deeply rooted in real-world application.
With a 100% placement rate, the programme equips 
participants with critical technical skills, workplace readiness, and the confidence to thrive in a competitive industry. More importantly, it creates pathways for sustainable careers and upward social mobility, often becoming a turning point not just for the individual, but for their entire family.
Kaushalya is more than a programme—it is a 
transformational journey. Most importantly, it is shaping India’s next generation of skilled, resilient, and future-ready talent.Lakshya programme

Employee Culture Survey 2026
Our people and culture continue to be central to TMPVL’s 
ability to deliver sustained performance and drive transformation across Passenger Vehicles (PV) and Electric Vehicles (EV). Guided by the culture pillars of Be Bold, Own It, Solve Together and Be Empathetic, the organisation remains focused on building a workplace that enables ownership, collaboration, and accountability.
The 2026 Culture Survey shows strong alignment and belief 
in the culture framework across both businesses, with high understanding and emotional connect (over 80%), reflecting clarity on direction and leadership intent.
In PV, the overall engagement and accountability remains 
stable, with culture understanding at around 82%. While action scores are relatively lower (around mid 60%), the insights have helped focus 2026 priorities on enhancing empowerment, clarifying decision rights, and embedding collaboration into everyday ways of working.
In EV, the survey reflects the energy and demands of a fast growing, innovation driven organisation. The feedback has reinforced priorities around leadership role modelling, agile decision making, visible recognition and sustainable workloads, supporting continued performance and talent continuity.
Across PV and EV, the focus for 2026-27 is on further 
empowering teams, strengthening leadership ownership of culture, celebrating the right behaviours and enabling simpler, more effective cross functional collaboration. These priorities are being taken forward with clear intent and regular review, reinforcing progress and building sustained positive momentum across the organisation.
Together, these efforts demonstrate TMPVL’s ongoing 
commitment to nurturing a strong, inclusive and performance oriented culture that supports sustainable growth and long term value creation.

=== page 107 ===
Organisational effectiveness 
Project Odyssey: A seamless transition built on 
transparency and execution excellence with people at the core 
The Project Odyssey (demerger of Tata Motors) represented 
a pivotal transformation in our organisational journey, executed with a strong emphasis on structured change management, people continuity, and organisational effectiveness. The transition was anchored in transparency, proactive communication, and leadership alignment, ensuring that employees remained informed, engaged, and confident throughout the process. A multi-layered communication framework—comprising leadership townhalls, manager-led cascades, and digital platforms—enabled consistent messaging and real-time resolution of employee queries. Over 45,000 employees were seamlessly transitioned into new legal entities with minimal disruption, achieving zero-error in transition with full continuity of business-as-usual from Day 1, 100% accuracy across all the key HR processes, and zero non-compliance instances, supported by robust systems, harmonised policies, and strong governance.

Reward and recognition culture
Structured reward and recognition programmes have 
been rolled out across organisational levels to promote safe behaviours, recognise safety excellence, and drive continuous engagement in safety initiatives.
Future ready safety standards
To address evolving operational and regulatory requirements, 16 revised safety standards and 4 new standards were introduced, strengthening alignment with best practices and reinforcing a future ready safety governance framework.
Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA)
At TMPVL/TPEML risk assessment is done through Hazard Identification & Risk Assessment (HIRA) standard. HIRA standard guides the assessment methodology for each of the activities in the manufacturing operations.
Hazards at workplace are identified through HIRA for all 
routine activities/sub-activities. Cross functional team is formed to brainstorm & identify all hazards. All activities at TMPVL/TPEML are mapped and hazards are identified for each of these activities’ basis nature of activity, history of incidents and experience of workers. For all such identified hazards, risk is calculated based on Severity and Likelihood. Unit of measure of risk is Risk Priority Number (RPN).
Every hazard is categorised into Trivial, Tolerable, Moderate, 
Substantial and Intolerable. These hazards are then mitigated using hierarchy of controls. 
For non-routine activities risk assessment is done through Job 
safety analysis (JSA) which in itself is a separate standard.
The Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) process 
is tightly integrated into safety governance and operational decision making, with focused application in emerging and high risk domains such as EV battery handling. This integrated approach positions TMPVL/TPEML as future ready, risk resilient, and aligned with evolving technological and regulatory landscapes.

Addressing malnutrition in communities
In Moraiya village of Sanand, 4-year-old Ruhani Chauhan 
was among 23 children identified as malnourished. At 9.98 kg, Ruhani was enrolled in the ‘Kuposhan thi Suposhan’ child health initiative, and supported with protein supplementation, nutritious dates, and regular milk intake to strengthen her diet alongside home-cooked meals. Her mother was also counselled on balanced nutrition and the importance of avoiding packaged foods. Over eight months, Ruhani’s weight increased to 12.35 kg, moving her into the healthy range, thus demonstrating the effectiveness of sustained nutritional support and informed caregiving.

communities – Employment, Entrepreneurship, CSR ProgrammesCase Study
From Wadi to Market: Jawhar’s farmers take charge 
of their harvest
When Tata Motors began the Integrated Village 
Development Programme in a single Gram Panchayat of Palghar in 2018, the intent was simple: development that stays. Today IVDP spans six Gram Panchayats in Jawhar — and has travelled to 103 Gram Panchayats across twenty districts in five states.
In Jawhar, livelihoods anchor that journey. Through the 
wadi agroforestry model around 15,000 farmers have undertaken mango and cashew plantation through MGNREGA convergence. Meanwhile other farmers have been supported with jasmine floriculture and cash crops like watermelon, chilli and cluster beans.
But a good harvest meant little while middlemen set the 
price. So Tata Motors and its implementing partner, BAIF, linked farmers to three Farmer Producing Organisations (FPO) in Jawhar, which is now 4,000–5,000 members strong. FPOs collect the produce from the farmers at 6-7 collection centres and sell it directly in city markets. In FY26 alone: nearly 200 quintals sold, ₹15–20 more earned per kilogram, accounting to ₹9,000 of additional income per farmer.
The middleman is gone. The margin now goes home.

Advancing inclusion through  
sustainable interventions 
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited has been at the forefront of advancing 
the Tata Group’s vision of Affirmative Action and equitable development. Aadhar, the Company’s Affirmative Action framework, ensures that inclusive growth is embedded as an organisational practice. Through a structured approach, Aadhar focuses on expanding access to opportunities for Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), women, and persons with disabilities (PwD), addressing systemic inequities across five key pillars—Education, Employability, Essential Enablers (through CSR), and Employment and Entrepreneurship (through business).
Our approach is rooted in the belief that inclusion must 
be intentional, measurable and integrated into systems. Aadhar is therefore embedded across programme design, community outreach and partnerships, while also shaping engagement within our value chain. This dual approach enables us to address systemic inequities while creating pathways for long term socioeconomic mobility. 
In FY26, 52% of our community engagement resources 
were dedicated to SC/ST communities. Our programmes thus prioritised underserved geographies and marginalised communities reaching 102 aspirational districts. 
Integrated Village Development Programme
The Integrated Village Development Programme (IVDP) is our marquee programme focussing on holistic development of tribal and marginalised rural communities. Since last eight years, it has evolved into a robust and replicable model for sustainable rural development with presence in 194 villages across five states. 
IVDP aims on enhancing livelihoods, building self-sufficient 
villages by emphasising on strengthening local governance and leveraging existing government schemes. In the Jawhar block of the Palghar district in Maharashtra, since year 2018 IVDP has reduced seasonal migration from 80% to 25%, while focused agri-based interventions have increased 
incomes by 55%. While in Gujarat, the programme has enabled over 5,000 people from underserved villages to benefit from access to government schemes. 
Enhancing employability of tribal students
During the year, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited partnered with the National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS) to provide quality education and enhance employability among the tribal students across the country. This collaboration enables students from Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) to get access to professional coaching for Engineering and Medical entrance through ENABLE Programme, and others to join Kaushalya, our flagship employability programme, equipping them with industry-relevant skills and improving their access to formal employment opportunities.
Dignity and livelihood for waste pickers 
Recognising the critical yet often informal role of waste pickers in urban ecosystems, the Company has partnered with Kashtakari Panchayat in Pimpri Chinchwad, Pune to uplift 8,000 families. The initiative focuses on improving health, occupational health and safety, enabling access to education for their children, and strengthening livelihood opportunities through skill development. With a presence in 194 villages across five states, the 
Integrated Village Development Programme (IVDP) has emerged as a catalyst for holistic transformation in rural communities, contributing to measurable improvements in overall well-being. Rooted in a strategic, convergence-led approach, the programme addresses a broad range of developmental challenges—spanning livelihood, income generation, health, water management, sanitation, and governance—through close alignment with government schemes and proactive engagement with local stakeholders. IVDP has facilitated alignment of 50 government schemes and mobilised resources of more than ₹20 crore while strengthening governance in the communities it serves. 
Transforming tribal hamlets in Maharashtra
A key milestone in this journey was the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding with the Government of Maharashtra in 2018. The approach has strengthened last-mile delivery, enhanced institutional efficiencies, and established a scalable framework for integrated rural development.
The programme has delivered sustained impact across 
six Gram Panchayats in Palghar, reaching over 15,000 individuals from tribal communities. Interventions span 13 Sustainable Development Goals and 9 thematic areas, reflecting a comprehensive, systems-led approach to village development. IVDP has contributed to measurable socio-economic outcomes. The focussed effort on agri-based interventions has led to 55% increase in income and creation of 22 lakhpati Kisans, including 6 women farmers. The programme has reduced seasonal migration in the Jawhar block from 80% to 25%, thus enhancing livelihood opportunities in this tribal belt of Jawhar.
In parallel, healthcare and nutrition interventions 
have led to 95% decline in malnutrition, improved sanitation practices and 100% institutional deliveries, thus strengthening last mile healthcare services. Water resource management initiatives have enhanced both drinking and irrigation water availability, enabling year-round access in several habitations and contributing to improved agricultural productivity.
The integration of technology has strengthened service 
delivery and local entrepreneurship. Initiatives such as E-Dost have enabled rural youth to access digital platforms, create livelihood opportunities, and bridge service gaps within their communities.
Expansion to other geographies
Following the success of the programme in Palghar, Maharashtra, the Company has expanded and replicated IVDP at other locations including Pune, Sanand, Pantnagar and Dharwad. Moving beyond the manufacturing locations, the IVDP has been replicated in the aspirational districts of Balrampur and Shravasti in Uttar Pradesh. 
IVDP 2.0 – From district to state-level programme
During the year, Tata Motors Foundation entered into a subsequent agreement with the Government of Maharashtra to launch IVDP 2.0 across 80 plus Gram Panchayats, primarily in aspirational blocks.  IVDP 2.0 seeks to establish a scalable template and replicable template of rural development that can be deployed at block, district, state, and national levels, with an increased focus on strengthening local governance systems and leverage 100% eligible Government schemes to deepen sustainable development outcomes.
Through IVDP, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles 
Limited continues to operationalise its Affirmative Action philosophy by enabling inclusive growth, strengthening community institutions, and building resilient rural ecosystems. The programme stands as a scalable and replicable model, reinforcing the Company’s commitment to creating long-term value for communities while fostering self-sufficient villages.IVDP: Replicating inclusive and sustainable rural developmentExtending Affirmative Action into the value chain

Through capacity-building, mentorship, and preferential procurement, these enterprises are supported and integrate into mainstream business ecosystems. 
Through Aadhar, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited 
is strengthening a development model where inclusion is integrated across both community interventions and business ecosystems to enable equitable access to opportunities and ensure that the benefits of growth are shared across all sections of society.

1 Carbon net zero
Climate change remains one of the defining strategic 
challenges of our time. The automotive sector plays a pivotal role in global emissions and, therefore, holds significant influence in accelerating the transition to a low-carbon economy. As a manufacturer of luxury vehicles, we recognise our responsibility to lead this transformation. Therefore, responding to this challenge is not simply an environmental obligation, it is a business imperative. 
Our ambition is to achieve net zero by 2039 across our 
direct product emissions, operations and supply chain. This ambition aligns with a 1.5
oC pathway and is underpinned 
by science-based targets that guide our decarbonisation pathway and ensure our actions align with the latest climate science. Our ambition reflects not only the scale of the challenge but the scale of the opportunity to redefine modern luxury through sustainability; strengthening our resilience, enhancing long-term competitiveness, and contributing meaningfully to a sustainable future.  
Reducing lifecycle emissions requires decisive action and 
continuous collaboration and innovation. Yet the speed of this transition will be shaped as much by consumer behaviour as by the efforts of manufacturers. An evolving regulatory environment and the ongoing development of charging infrastructure will be critical in influencing consumer confidence in electrification. 
These external factors introduce uncertainty that could 
significantly impact our ability to deliver against our mid-term science-based targets. To strengthen governance and transparency, we are developing a Climate Transition Plan that will enable us to communicate these risks effectively, demonstrate a credible pathway to net zero, and embed the appropriate internal oversight needed to deliver it. 
The following sections reflect our performance in FY26 as 
well as our key initiatives across our operational and product emissions. The reported results are in alignment with the scope of our Reporting Methodology Statement available on our corporate website. Reported Scope 1 and 2 data, therefore, only includes those sites which are within the scope of our SBTi reporting requirements.Operational emissions –  
Scope 1 and 2
Our operational emissions arise mainly from three sources: Scope 1 emissions produced by gas combustion for heat and power at our facilities and emissions from company-owned vehicles, and Scope 2 emissions associated with purchased electricity. Achieving net zero operational emissions will require us to cut energy use through greater efficiency, to transition to renewable electricity and to phase out gas consumption by electrifying our heat and energy systems. 
Performance
In FY26, our absolute Scope 1 and 2 emissions reduced to 221.3 ktCO
2e. This was an 11.3 per cent reduction compared 
to FY25 and a 32.1 per cent reduction compared to our location-based FY20 baseline, placing the results ahead of the required SBTi trajectory to be aligned to a 1.5
oC pathway 
(25.2%). The result was affected by the cyber incident during which production was paused for five weeks before restarting on 8 October. However, the remaining months still achieved a 29.5 per cent reduction compared to the equivalent baseline months in FY20.
Key initiatives
The significant reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions in FY26 was achieved through continued improvement in energy efficiency, particularly to heating and ventilation at key sites, as well as the installation of increased renewable energy capacity aligned with our strategic focus areas. 
1. Nitra, Slovakia, flue gas heat recovery 
The Nitra facility advanced its decarbonisation, roadmap through the installation, of a flue gas heat recovery system during summer 2025. This initiative captures and reuses waste heat from existing processes, reducing reliance on primary energy sources. The project represents a scalable model for energy efficiency improvements across the wider manufacturing network.

Supply chain and product  
emissions – Scope 3  
Our Scope 3 emissions are heavily influenced by the emissions produced when our vehicles are driven. Electrifying our portfolio is, therefore, fundamental to our science-based targets and realising our net zero ambition. A key milestone on this journey is our commitment for every brand to offer a pure-electric option by 2030, but progress toward these goals will rely on sustained consumer demand for battery electric vehicles. At the same time, we must avoid shifting emissions upstream into our supply chain by partnering with our suppliers to decarbonise key materials and expand the use of recycled content.
